questions.q: What does merging two queries do, conceptually?
options: Joins them sideways, based on a shared column, like a database join
Stacks them on top of each other, combining matching columns into more rows
Deletes duplicate rows between the two tables
Converts one table's data types to match the other
questions.explain: Merge pulls columns from one table into another based on a matching key column — different from Append (Lesson 21), which stacks tables with the same columns.

questions.q: Which two join kinds cover the vast majority of real-world merges?
options: Left outer and Inner
Left anti and Right anti
Full outer and Right outer
There's no meaningful difference between any of the six
questions.explain: Left outer (keep everything from the main table, enrich where possible) and Inner (keep only rows that matched in both tables) handle most practical merging needs. The anti joins are specialty tools for finding unmatched rows.

questions.q: After merging two tables, what does the new column in your left table initially contain?
options: A nested [Table] value for each row, which you expand to pull out specific fields
The actual expanded columns immediately, with no further steps needed
An error, until you manually fix the join
A count of how many rows matched
questions.explain: The merge creates one new column holding a nested table value per row. You use the expand icon on that column to choose which fields from the right table to bring in as real columns.

questions.q: In a Left Outer join, why might a row show null in the newly merged columns?
options: That row's key value had no match in the right table
Null always means a data type error occurred
It means the merge itself failed
Nulls only appear with Inner joins, never Left Outer
questions.explain: Left Outer keeps every row from the left table regardless of whether it matched. When there's no match in the right table, the merged columns come back null — which is informative, not an error.

questions.q: If you only want rows that matched in both tables, discarding anything that didn't match either side, which join kind do you use?
options: Inner
Left anti
Full outer
Left outer
questions.explain: Inner join keeps only rows with a match in both the left and right tables — everything else is dropped.
